clue.text: Finding a drug upset the warder

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prison officer is discovered to have smuggled drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' shuffles A DRUG; 'Finding' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard is a prison officer, the same job as a warder.

clue.text: Bearing with fish smell

parts.note: a compass bearing, here south, abbreviated S
the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone notices an odour coming from fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, unpleasant odour.

clue.text: These fliers scrap over others

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed over another comes first

parts.note: a scrap is a small bit
the other fliers are terns, seabirds

explanation.surface: Birds fighting over other birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight but is a small piece; 'others' means other birds, here terns.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterns are marsh birds of the heron family.

clue.text: Old serving man giving vent maybe — about time!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the period
maybe signals the letters of vent are only one possible arrangement

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An old soldier finally lets off steam after a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vent maybe' reads as letting off steam, but 'maybe' signals an anagram; 'about' wraps the shuffle round the time word, and 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is a former member of the armed forces, someone who once served.

clue.text: Hang on to small-page book

parts.note: page abbreviates to p, written as a small (lower-case) letter
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: Someone clings to a tiny pocket book.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to keep it, holding on to it.

clue.text: Not paid, so likely to make a change

definitions.meaning: ... weather or circumstances are liable to alter

explanation.definitionFit: Unsettled means both outstanding (of a debt) and changeable or unstable.

clue.text: American backing composer, he's really supportive

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Sir John Stainer was an English composer of church music

explanation.surface: An American championing a composer is a loyal fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sustains others holds them up, giving support.

clue.text: Carry a key ring

parts.note: B is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone carries a key ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something is to carry it along.

clue.text: A cut some people approach optimistically

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so the answer is a run of letters lying inside the following words

explanation.surface: A cut of meat that some diners look forward to.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a whole cryptic definition, but the answer sits across the end of 'approach' and the start of 'optimistically'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop is a cutting blow, or a cut of meat.

clue.text: Animal circumventing snare in the dark

indicators.note: circumventing means going round, so the beast surrounds the trap

parts.note: a brute is a beast
a net is a snare

explanation.surface: A creature skirting a trap in darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette is a woman with dark hair, the dark one rather than the fair.

clue.text: Accommodation (not 5-star) for those unfortunately left behind

indicators.note: behind places the letter after the anagram
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of those are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cheap lodgings for the unlucky ones left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostel offers cheap, basic lodging, far from luxury.

clue.text: Burn to do odd jobs?

definitions.meaning: to scorch or blacken the surface
to work as a cleaner doing housework

explanation.definitionFit: Char means scorch, and also to clean houses as a charwoman.

clue.text: A skinhead-lawless individual but sound

parts.note: the head of the word skin is its first letter
a pirate is an outlaw of the sea

explanation.surface: A skinhead is a lawless sort, but healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'healthy' but is a noun: a breathed sound like H.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirate is a breathed consonant, as in phonetics.

clue.text: His response to complaint is always simple

definitions.text: His response to complaint is always simple

parts.words: His response to complaint is always simple
parts.note: complaint means an illness, and a simple is an old word for a medicinal plant remedy

explanation.surface: Someone who always answers grumbles plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist treats illnesses with plant remedies, once called simples.

clue.text: Most intimate article about going into a home

indicators.note: going into means placed inside, so the two short pieces sit within the home

parts.note: a nest is a home
a is the indefinite article
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A very personal piece about moving into a new house.
explanation.definitionFit: The nearest friends are the closest, most intimate ones.

clue.text: A riot can result in personal protection being obtained

indicators.note: result in suggests the letters produce something new when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Unrest leads to people needing protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is part of the letters to shuffle; 'being obtained' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A raincoat protects the wearer from rain, worn on the person.

clue.text: Looked up to, though perpetually in debt

indicators.note: in places the word for always inside the word for debt

parts.note: in the red means in debt
ever means always or perpetually

explanation.surface: Someone admired despite always owing money.
explanation.definitionFit: Revered means deeply respected, admired.

clue.text: Aim to consume a little cod. It's approved of

indicators.note: to consume means to swallow, so the aim takes the fish inside

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
a dorse is a young cod

explanation.surface: Someone aiming to eat a bit of fish says it is good.
explanation.walkthrough: DORSE, an old word for a young cod, is little known.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorsed means backed or sanctioned.

clue.text: Writing cagily?

parts.note: writing with a pen, and also shutting animals up in a pen or cage

explanation.surface: Writing guardedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Penning means composing in writing and also confining animals in an enclosure.

clue.text: Thin base for making alcoholic drink

indicators.note: for making signals the letters are used to build something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weak foundation for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green spirit flavoured with wormwood.

clue.text: Go off and twist

definitions.meaning: to go sour, as milk does

explanation.definitionFit: Turn means to sour (of milk) and to rotate.

clue.text: Such stuff conveys nothing to a sportsman

definitions.text: Such stuff conveys nothing to a sportsman

parts.words: Such stuff conveys nothing to a sportsman
parts.note: stuffed fowl reads as a meal, but in cricket a score of zero has the same name

explanation.surface: A remark that some material means nothing to an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter out without scoring has made a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A duck is a bird, cooked stuffed, and a cricket score of nothing.

clue.text: Roughly, roughly a score

definitions.note: an adverb standing for the adjective rough, crude

indicators.note: roughly means approximately, so the letters are only loosely in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: About twenty, approximately.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adverb for an adjective, a looseness of the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means rough in texture or manners.

clue.text: Relaxed, having invested money in wine

indicators.note: having invested means putting money into something, so the money goes inside the wine

parts.note: sack is an old type of sherry
L is the pound, money

explanation.surface: Someone at ease after putting money into wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack means loose or not tight.

clue.text: Battered relics found in the kitchen

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Damaged antiques turn up among the cooking things.
explanation.definitionFit: A slicer is a kitchen utensil for cutting food.

clue.text: There's no fighting force to join usually

parts.note: RM is the Royal Marines
to ally is to join forces

explanation.surface: There is no army to sign up to, as is normal.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally means as a rule, in the ordinary way.

clue.text: Experiment with arsenic for example

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
say means for example

explanation.surface: Trials with a poisonous element.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is a test or trial of a metal or substance.

clue.text: To bury some church members cross is required

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a sect is a group of church members

explanation.surface: A cross is needed for a church burial.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersect is to cross each other.
